extracted.intended_audience: EU grant applicants whose proposal was rejected (users of the Funding & Tenders Portal)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for applicants on how and when to challenge a rejected proposal under the EU Funding & Tenders Portal: available redress routes, deadlines, what complaints may or may not raise, and procedural consequences of reviews/re-evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds to submit a complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: You may submit a complaint if you believe that the rejection of your proposal was based on an error in the selection procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the deadlines and procedures set out in the evaluation result letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Available means of redress and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally available remedies include: request for admissibility/eligibility or evaluation review (redress review); request for review of legality under Article 22 of Regulation 58/2003 for decisions by EU executive agencies; and action for annulment under Article 263 TFEU.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadlines: redress review — within 30 days of receiving the letter; Article 22 (for executive agencies) — within 1 month of receiving the letter (use the Article 22 complaints form template); action for annulment under Article 263 TFEU — within 2 months of receiving the letter. You are free to choose any of these means of redress, but administrative review procedures are recommended first.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation to use administrative review first
rubrics_metrics.description: In the interest of good administration and procedural efficiency, it is recommended to first use available administrative review procedures (if any).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The objective of administrative review procedures is to re-examine the circumstances of the selection procedure and to reach a final decision on your application. Deadlines for further redress will run from when you receive the reply with the final position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of admissible complaints (focus on evaluation, not merits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Complaints must focus on aspects concerning the evaluation of the proposals (e.g. admissibility or eligibility checks, evaluation procedure), not their merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants can raise procedural irregularities, factual errors, manifest errors of assessment or abuse of powers. Examples given: lack of coherence between scores and comments, lack or inadequate reasoning of the conclusions, existence of a conflict of interests, exceeding the limits of discretion, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: What will not be considered
rubrics_metrics.description: Mere repetitions of the content of the proposal or disagreements with the result or reasoning of the technical evaluation will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A complaint must show procedural/factual/manifest errors or abuse of power — simple disagreement is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single review request limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Only one request for review per proposal will be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request cannot refer to the evaluation of proposals submitted by other applicants or under different or previous calls.

rubrics_metrics.name: When re-evaluation will (or will not) be ordered
rubrics_metrics.description: Review requests will not always necessarily lead to a re-evaluation of your proposal. The administrative review will re-examine your case, but a re-evaluation will be decided only if your complaint demonstrates that the procedural irregularity, factual error, manifest error of assessment or abuse of powers affects the decision on whether to fund the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For example, a problem relating to one evaluation criterion will not lead to a re-evaluation if, even by adding the maximum points under this criterion, the final score would still remain below the threshold for funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-evaluation scope and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Any re-evaluation will be made on the proposal as it was originally submitted; no additional information will be admitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Re-evaluations will be partial (limited to the criterion affected by the error) or full (when the whole evaluation has been recognized as flawed) — depending on the case. They may be assigned to the same evaluation panel or a new one, depending on the internal procedures of the Granting Authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential outcomes of re-evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: The score following a re-evaluation may be lower than the original score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be aware that re-evaluation can change the score downward as well as upward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of review requests
rubrics_metrics.description: All requests for review will be treated as confidential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct addressee for complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: Pay attention to who took the formal decision and who the complaint must be addressed to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a decision was taken by an EU executive agency or other EU body, both redress review and applications for annulment must be directed against that agency/body (NOT against the European Commission). Only Article 22 complaints must be addressed to the respective Directorate‑General of the Commission (parent DG of the executive agency).

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to complain to the European Ombudsman for maladministration
rubrics_metrics.description: If you consider there has been maladministration, you can also address a complaint to the European Ombudsman.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadline: within 2 years after you became aware of it AND after having used all the means of administrative redress available (redress and Article 22 request, if any).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification access rule affecting deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Notifications which have not been opened within 10 days after sending are considered to have been accessed and the deadlines will be counted from opening/access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Portal Terms and Conditions for details; applicants are responsible for monitoring notifications.
